findings.title: PUBLIC-DEPLOYMENT.md §3.1's PostgreSQL block omits ZECK_ENVIRONMENT — a stranger following the block literally hits deploy:migrate's fail-closed environment contract and a release cascade
findings.reproduction: Follow §3.1's PostgreSQL block exactly: export ZECK_PG_ADMIN_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres (the block's only export) → bun run deploy:bootstrap -- --environment local (exit 0, but environmentContract.satisfied=false with 'ZECK_ENVIRONMENT is required and not set' reported in the output) → bun run deploy:migrate -- --environment local → EXIT 2 'error: the environment contract is not satisfied: ZECK_ENVIRONMENT is required (the environment identity this process represents); ZECK_ENVIRONMENT is required and not set'; with the schema never created, deploy:release record/gate/promote each EXIT 1 'relation release_control.releases does not exist' and the guardrails evaluation falls back to the honest fresh-database empty set. The same section's provision line teaches the variable only in per-command form (ZECK_ENVIRONMENT=local bun run deploy:provision …) which does not persist into the following block. The DEP-040 e2e driver never hits this because IT sets ZECK_ENVIRONMENT for its chain steps — the doc's path and the driver's path differ exactly here (recorded in reproductionRun.docVsDriverDifference).
findings.disposition: GATE FINDING (PUBLIC-DEPLOYMENT.md is outside this order's writable surface — docs/DEVELOPER-PLATFORM-DELIVERY-REPORT.md, deploy/evidence/dep-044.json and roadmap status annotations only). RECOMMENDED CLOSURE (Lead's call, trivial class): add 'export ZECK_ENVIRONMENT=local' to §3.1's PostgreSQL block (one line). This session verified the recovery: with the variable exported, the ENTIRE chain runs green end to end (reproductionRun.recoverySegment — 9/9 steps, migrate 33/33, promote verified at HEAD, teardown verified GONE).

freeTierPosture.summary: The provider topology maximizes free-tier use under the doctrine order (provider free tier → usage-based/no-minimum → low fixed-cost managed → paid only where required), with every selection's rationale, limits, degradation path and upgrade/exit note recorded in deploy/manifests/provider-tiers.json (asOf 2026-09-16). Four of eight concerns ride provider FREE TIERS (Neon Free — the authoritative relational store; Cloudflare R2 free allowances — artifact bytes; Upstash Redis Free — ephemeral coordination; Vercel Hobby — experience delivery). Three ride USAGE-BASED/NO-MINIMUM tiers because no free tier exists for their production shape (Cloudflare Queues, Cloudflare Workflows, any OTLP collector). One is PAID-WHERE-REQUIRED by a safety/capability constraint (the zeck-container-runner: execution compute is a governed authority concern — self-hosted/governed, never a disposable free resource). The commercial-terms constraint is explicit: Vercel Hobby is non-commercial-only (the hard rule in PUBLIC-DEPLOYMENT.md §2); commercial production must upgrade or rehost — the API is independently runnable so hosting moves with configuration only. Free-tier disposability is enforced structurally: every free-tier dependency carries an upgrade/exit note and 'disposable free-tier resources never become operationally critical' is the doctrine — PROVEN operationally by the DEP-043 provider-exit drill (all 8 classes: the executed backup/restore round-trip, the repoint proof with byte-identical identity documents, the degraded postures attested live; every live half honest NOT RUN with owner). Zero live cost was consumed across the entire program (no provider credentials ever existed in a worker pod). The one open boundary: live verification of the recorded limits (providerTierVerification 'recorded-not-live-verified') — the credentialed operator re-verifies each limit before applying the deployment.
